findings.risk: The private actor pass with validateWorld=false omits both prop validation and the model-exit comparison. In validatePropBindings, the sourceOwnership branch throws before world validation, source bindings and alias coverage; the sourceManipulation branch throws before the remaining per-binding checks. Valid ownership alone, or an expected production rejection, therefore cannot establish complete candidate correctness.
findings.requiredConstraint: The strict candidate path must independently establish every applicable original ownership, world, binding, alias, owner identity/stage/clock and source-evidence constraint before entering the private actor pass. Bindings not covered by validated original-source semantics must retain their existing contract. Compare continuity.models against modelExitParts using the original complete context. Never convert a caught needs-source-prop-binding exception into candidate success.

findings.risk: phaseBoard supplies merged context, but acting coverage is suppressed for fragments and continuity iterates board.shots, not phaseBoard.shots. A fragment can consequently omit its actual adjacent cuts. The camera membership check proves only one matching shot ID/hash; it does not prove that the supplied board or narration is complete and authoritative.
findings.requiredConstraint: Establish authoritative complete board/narration identity separately from shot membership. Complete-board acting coverage and continuity must remain required, including both boundaries around each fragment. Candidate fragments must be exact unique members of that immutable board, not substitutions that acquire authority merely through phaseBoard merging.

findings.risk: Sharing the explainer checker does not automatically share final-direction validation: it does not invoke requireFinalStoryDirection. That separate function rejects missing semantic acting, unsupported actions or missing manipulation/indication targets, unaccepted canonical cast planning, and absent/offline art direction.
findings.requiredConstraint: The complete-board diagnostic must explicitly retain these final-direction checks. An ApprovalRequired exception must become a recorded diagnostic failure, never an approval transition or a reason to omit the check. Passing these source checks must not imply artwork or motion acceptance.

findings.risk: cameraSubjects can throw before a report exists, and inspectCastCameras returns immediately with only a world issue when ownershipScene fails. Thus even this collecting diagnostic does not always examine every actor. It also requires canonical non-sprite shots. A fail-fast storyboard rejection could further prevent separate camera findings from being recorded.
findings.requiredConstraint: Record camera diagnostics independently of earlier storyboard/source failures. Distinguish checked, failed, blocked and not-applicable scope; unexamined actors must never count as passing. Preserve ownership and exact-membership requirements rather than removing them to obtain camera reports. Respect the canonical-rig-only precondition and retain production validation for other rows.

requiredInvariants: The existing exported production explainer entry point must always retain production cinematic validation. Candidate selection and any internal validation substitution must not become caller-controlled skip flags.

Original board, narration, world shot and actual person clock must remain explicit throughout candidate validation, supporting-actor validation, interaction checks, model continuity and camera diagnostics.
Source classification must include applicable ownership, world and primary/supporting manipulation data; non-source rows in the same complete board must retain production validation.
Preserve all existing source, actor, voice, contact and production gates. Keep needs-source-prop-binding intact on production paths.
Every candidate report must retain productionReady:false, productionRig:null, availableBanks:[], canPublish:false and all approval flags false, regardless of source-check results.
Associate checks, failures and blocked checks with exact input receipts. Parsed semantic inputs must not silently replace the identity of the original input being reported.
The proposed read-only diagnostic must not save artifacts, change approval/state, mark DONE, or initiate production. Receipt changes must invalidate the diagnostic rather than bless stale results.

findings.trigger: For a shot with actual primary or supporting actors, `inspectCastCameras(shot, profile, board, narration)` throws before returning its actor rows—for example, when a camera/world dependency failure is thrown rather than returned as an issue.
findings.impact: The catch records only a shot-level `unavailable` check. The actual actors in that shot receive no actor-specific `unavailable` checks, contrary to the diagnostic requirement that uninspected actual actors be marked unavailable when camera/source inspection fails.
findings.correction: In the catch, derive the actual actor IDs from `shot.cinematic?.actorScene` and append one `cast-camera` `unavailable` check per actor, including the caught error message; retain a shot-level check only when there are no actual actors.
